# Two Truths, One Lie

A Skill Harbor house build: Two Truths, One Lie, the bluffing icebreaker classic, refereed by your own Muse inside a group chat you own. Players take turns as the featured player. Each featured player privately gives the referee three short statements about themselves, two true and one false, and the game turns on a simple pleasure: learning surprising true things about people you know, and finding out who can bluff with a plausible detail. It plays with 3 players minimum, 4 to 8 recommended, and it is asynchronous on purpose: collection runs 24 hours by default and voting 12 hours, so a turn takes hours and a full cycle, every player featured exactly once in the recorded rotation order, stretches over days around real life.

Your assistant is the referee, and the sealing is the whole design. The three statements are collected in private, in a 1:1 thread with the featured player, who designates in that same private reply which statement is the lie. Before anything is published, the referee runs a written quality gate: all three statements must be plausible and comparably detailed, verifiable in principle, short and self-contained, with nothing sensitive (health, money, intimate life, conflicts, third parties). A sensitive or unverifiable statement, a pure taste or opinion nobody could be right or wrong about, is replaced before publication, privately, and the request gives only the gate reason: it never reveals, in any message, which statement is the lie.
